Yes—probably.

At **3.75° altitude**, the Moon is geometrically above the **east-southeastern horizon** (azimuth **113°**) by roughly **7–8 apparent Moon diameters**. With **43% illumination**, a clear, fully dark sky, and knowledge of where to look, it should be conspicuous **if you have an unobstructed horizon**.

The main caveat is Denver’s local terrain and buildings: at such a low altitude, even a modest ridge, tree line, building, or atmospheric haze could hide it. Refraction may lift its apparent position slightly, but extinction near the horizon will dim and redden it.

So, unfortunately given your hope: **from an open site with a clear ESE horizon, you would likely be able to see it; from many ordinary urban locations, it could easily be blocked.** It would also be close to setting, so visibility would not last long.
